Pcp-elements -- elements of a pc-presented group
A pcp-element is an element of a group defined by a consistent pc-presentation given by a collector. Suppose that g_1, \ldots, g_n are the defining generators of the collector with relative orders r_1, \ldots, r_n, and let I be the set of indices i with r_i \neq 0. Recall that each element g in this group can be written uniquely as a collected word g_1^{e_1} \cdots g_n^{e_n} with e_i \in &ZZ; and 0 \leq e_i < r_i for i \in I. The integer vector [e_1, \ldots, e_n] is called the exponent vector of g.
More generally, any integer vector [e_1, \ldots, e_n] describes the element g_1^{e_1} \cdots g_n^{e_n}, and any generator exponent list [i_1, e_1, \ldots, i_k, e_k] as introduced in Chapter describes the element g_{i_1}^{e_1} \cdots g_{i_k}^{e_k}. Such a vector or list is in normal form if it is the one obtained from a collected word:
an integer vector [e_1, \ldots, e_n] is in normal form if it has length n and 0 \leq e_i < r_i for all i \in I;
a generator exponent list [i_1, e_1, \ldots, i_k, e_k] is in normal form if i_1 < \cdots < i_k, all e_j are non-zero, and 0 < e_j < r_{i_j} whenever i_j \in I.
Thus the exponent vector of an element, as returned by , and its generator exponent list, as returned by , are always in normal form.
The following functions define pcp-elements from integer vectors or generator exponent lists. The versions without NC accept arbitrary input and collect it. The NC versions do not collect: they require input in normal form and return an invalid element otherwise.

PcpElementByExponents accepts any integer vector of length n. PcpElementByExponentsNC requires exp to be in normal form.

In the following example g_1 has relative order 2 and g_2 has infinite order, so [3, 5] and [2, 1, 1, 1] are not in normal form. The last line shows the invalid result of passing such input to an NC function.
gap> G := DihedralPcpGroup( 0 );; gap> coll := Collector( G );; gap> RelativeOrders( coll ); [ 2, 0 ] gap> PcpElementByExponents( coll, [ 3, 5 ] ); g1*g2^5 gap> PcpElementByGenExpList( coll, [ 2, 1, 1, 1 ] ); g1*g2^-1 gap> PcpElementByExponentsNC( coll, [ 1, 5 ] ); g1*g2^5 gap> PcpElementByGenExpListNC( coll, [ 1, 1, 2, -1 ] ); g1*g2^-1 gap> PcpElementByGenExpListNC( coll, [ 2, 1, 1, 1 ] ); g1*g2
These functions return pcp-elements in the category IsPcpElement. Presently, the only representation implemented for this category is IsPcpElementRep. (This allows us to be a little sloppy right now. The basic set of operations for IsPcpElement has not been defined yet. This is going to happen in one of the next version, certainly as soon as the need for different representations arises.)

Methods for pcp-elements
Now we can describe attributes and functions for pcp-elements. The four basic attributes of a pcp-element, Collector, Exponents, GenExpList and NameTag are computed at the creation of the pcp-element. All other attributes are determined at runtime.
Let g be a pcp-element and g_1, \ldots, g_n a polycyclic generating sequence of the underlying pc-presented group. Let C_1, \ldots, C_n be the polycyclic series defined by g_1, \ldots, g_n.
The depth of a non-trivial element g of a pcp-group (with respect to the defining generators) is the integer i such that g \in C_i \setminus C_{i+1}. The depth of the trivial element is defined to be n+1. If g\not=1 has depth i and g_i^{e_i} \cdots g_n^{e_n} is the collected word for g, then e_i is the leading exponent of g.
If g has depth i, then we call r_i = [C_i:C_{i+1}] the factor order of g. If r < \infty, then the smallest positive integer l with g^l \in C_{i+1} is the called relative order of g. If r=\infty, then the relative order of g is defined to be 0. The index e of \langle g,C_{i+1}\rangle in C_i is called relative index of g. We have that r = el.
We call a pcp-element normed, if its leading exponent is equal to its relative index. For each pcp-element g there exists an integer e such that g^e is normed.
